name: Gate → ESCALATE: park the exhausted/unprovable task toward the human
description:
The escalate router (design SB4/SB5, group 7D). When check_gate derives ESCALATE — the attempt was not clean AND the iteration budget is exhausted (distinct task.attempt.<i> count >= task.spec.<i>.budget), OR a required gate fact was missing (check_gate fails CLOSED toward escalate) — the dev loop cannot converge by rule. This rule PARKS the run toward the human: it records run.awaiting_human on the run and posts to the channel-agnostic user-response bus. No Go reconciler, backstop ticker, or app-side state machine advances a run whose dev loop exhausted its budget (G2/B3/B7); the human sees the detailed dev.gate.<i>.reason check_gate stamped. This is the honest terminal of the bounded loop — the semspec disease inverted: an unconverged task NEVER passes verify or ships a hollow PR, it parks.

WRITER: run.awaiting_human's writer is the park-rule subsystem (G5) — the THIRD realization of that single logical writer, alongside run-lifecycle/03 (a coordinator ask_human decision) and sandbox/02 (an unprovable sandbox). All three mean the identical thing (this run awaits a human, here is why) and upsert the one park marker the whole system reads (the D15 park-exclusion forward-contract keys on run.awaiting_human); they differ only in TRIGGER. Rule add_triple carries no Source, so the vocab keeps the single run.awaiting_human entry with no runtime writer drift.

TRIGGER = the check_gate LOOP terminal via the dev.gate_decision loop marker. Fires on agent.loop.role=coordinator AND dev.gate_decision eq "escalate" — a single LITERAL eq (#519-immune), mutually exclusive with the advance/retry routers on the single decision value.

RUN BINDING: the park marker goes on the RUN (subject-override $entity.triple.agent.run.entity_id — the gate loop carries the run anchor), so the whole system reads the park on the run. Unlike sandbox/02 (which fires on the run and stamps $entity.id), this fires on the gate LOOP and redirects, exactly like run-lifecycle/03.

SELF-EXTINGUISHING ONE-SHOT (restart-safe): on_enter FIRST stamps dev.routed=$entity.instance on the gate loop, guarded by dev.routed length_eq 0. This LOOP-scoped guard is required (not a run.awaiting_human guard) because this rule fires on the gate loop, which does NOT carry run.awaiting_human (that lives on the run) — a run-scoped guard would always read absent on the loop and re-post to the user bus every rescan. The shared dev.routed marker fires the park exactly once per gate loop.

on_enter.subject: $entity.triple.agent.run.entity_id
on_enter.object: the dev loop exhausted its iteration budget without a clean attempt (or a gate fact was missing); see dev.gate.0.reason

metadata.station: route escalate — park the exhausted/unprovable task toward the human (SB4/SB5, 7D)
metadata.trigger_rationale: fires on the check_gate loop's dev.gate_decision marker with a LITERAL eq "escalate" — #519-immune, mutually exclusive with advance/retry.
metadata.writer_note: run.awaiting_human is written by the park-rule subsystem (G5) — this is a THIRD realization of that single logical writer (same predicate, same meaning), sharing it with run-lifecycle/03 and sandbox/02. Rule add_triple carries no Source, so the vocab's single run.awaiting_human entry is not drifted.
metadata.restart_safe: SELF-EXTINGUISHING via the LOOP-scoped dev.routed marker + length_eq 0 guard. A LOOP guard (not run.awaiting_human) is REQUIRED here because the rule fires on the gate loop, which does not carry the run-scoped park marker — a run-scoped guard would never extinguish and would re-post to the user bus each rescan.
metadata.fail_closed: check_gate escalates on budget exhaustion OR a missing judgment fact (fail closed, never a false retry). Either way the loop parks honestly — an unconverged task never reaches verify or a PR (the class both predecessors faked).
